newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's king in Gaza after Hebron talks fail.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king in Gaza after Hebron talks fail.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein held talks in Gaza with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday after the United States said its peace envoy was leaving the region without an Israel-PLO deal on the West Bank town of Hebron.

"King Hussein is here to say that implementing the agreement (on Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron) is a very important step in making the whole peace process work," Palestinian Planning Minister Nabil Shaath told reporters.
"His personal influence and the influence of his country on Israel should be important," Shaath said.

It was the Jordanian monarch's first visit to self-ruled Gaza. Jordanian officials said he would express support for the Palestinians over the long overdue Israeli partial pullback in Hebron and further army redeployments from the West Bank.

King Hussein, Israel's closest Arab ally in the months following his 1994 peace treaty with the Jewish state, has distanced himself from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over policies that include support for Jewish settlement expansion.
U.S. embassy spokesman Richard Scorza told Reuters that U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross would leave for home later on Sunday.
Ross arrived three weeks ago to try again to forge a deal to launch Palestinian self-rule in 80 percent of Hebron, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.
The talks have hit an impasse over a timetable for Israeli withdrawals in rural areas of the West Bank following the Hebron pullback.

"He feels that the mediation role has been achieved, the assignment is complete," Scorza said. Asked if Ross's mission had failed for lack of an agreement, he said: "It's up to the parties to make the deal."
Arafat's cabinet said in a statement on Saturday: "The talks are close to a dead end."

Israel was due to have completed the Hebron handover 10 months ago. But violence, security concerns, and other issues have held up a deal. Some 400 Jews and 100,000 Arabs live in the town, holy to both as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.

King Hussein landed at Arafat's office in Gaza City after Israel refused a Palestinian request to receive the monarch's helicopter at an airport in the south of the strip. Israel demands security control of the airport.
"This is a great honour and encouragement from him to push the peace process forward and to strengthen the Palestinian-Jordanian relationship," Arafat told Israel Radio earlier on Sunday.
King Hussein and Arafat have a history of uneasy relations, but Arab frustration with Netanyahu appears to have brought them closer together.

The monarch became the first Arab head of state to visit the Palestinian self-ruled areas when he met Arafat in the West Bank enclave of Jericho last October. It was his first visit to the West Bank since Israel seized it from Jordan in a 1967 war.
The king was accompanied by Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.
Arafat and King Hussein planned to have Iftar together, the meal at dusk that Moslems take after fasting during daylight hours in the holy month of Ramadan.
Arafat's cabinet said in a statement on Saturday: "If the international community does not move immediately to save the peace process...then the whole region will witness explosions."

It said Israel was violating its 1995 interim peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation by demanding that future West Bank withdrawals, due to be completed by September 1997, be put off until May 1999.
Palestinians have rejected a U.S. compromise proposal that Israel complete further West Bank withdrawals by 1998.
